hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $2$.
And the point at $2$ is *not* filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything strictly **greater than $2$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**


[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 2. A line running to the right starts at 2 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < 2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 2. A line running to the left starts at 2 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/8cb2d0321f4ae95a88cf86fbae91e6932225b57b)

The graph of $x \leq 2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A closed point is plotted at 2. A line running to the left starts at 2 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/574460c88aba224e8bdf0b9eec18a6d3cca3b4f3)

The graph of $x \geq 2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A closed point is plotted at 2. A line running to the right starts at 2 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e4a006725cf24d80507780b664cd6b95a785f2e0)
